scope: New product restore interleaving finding; prior activation/observer fixes and actual38 controlled checks remain valid at their original scope. Not a rerun or completefeature review.

findings.title: Do not overwrite edits made while an asynchronous restore is pending
trigger: An existing empty conversation view has a retained saved draft. Select Restore without sending; RecoveryWorkspace validates the saved record then marks the view restoring.

App checks existing text/knowledge/files before awaiting projection.refresh. Delay that read; close the recovery dialog and enter new composer text or change intent/profile. Closing the dialog does not cancel the pending restore, and the Thread/controls have no restore lease gating edits.
Composer subscription writes the new text into drafts; RecoveryWorkspace.changed returns immediately while restoring, so that new value is not saved or marked pending.

When projection.refresh resolves, App current() checks authorization/generation only. It then writes saved.text and saved.profile, sets saved.intent/restoredVersion, causing the official composer effect to replace the new local text. No post-await material revision check preserves that edit.
evidence: apps/web/src/recovery/binding.tsx:171 changed returns for restoring; :282–292 restore marks the whole awaited host.restore as restoring; close only publishes open:false.
apps/web/src/App.tsx:680 current-material guard precedes projection.refresh at693; :707–710 overwrite full draft fields with no local-material revalidation.
apps/web/src/conversations/ConversationThread.tsx:182–188 subscribes composer changes into drafts; restoredVersion effect writes drafts back into official composer.
RecoverySurface close and restore buttons provide no per-view busy/ownership token; sendReason checks authorization/plugin only.
findings.impact: New unsaved text can be silently replaced by the older record; ignored changed notifications mean it need not exist in durable storage. This is source-demonstrated interleaving, not an executed browser failure.
findings.requestedFix: Use the existing per-view Recovery/App ownership seam to prevent an in-flight restore from replacing material that changed after capture. Revalidate full local draft revision/identity after awaited work and before synchronous application, or enforce a complete per-view restoring lease consistently across all mutating controls and actions. Preserve and checkpoint new material on conflict/abort; do not simply add a text-only check or new global state store. Keep explicit restore and original receipt rules, no automatic command dispatch.
acceptance: Deferred restore + edit text during wait: newer text survives and is checkpointable; stale saved record stays intact, clear conflict or cancellation is reported, zero command POST.
Same pattern for intent/profile-only changes; complete draft guard covers all saved fields.
Unchanged target succeeds and normal initialization notifications do not falsely conflict; auth/generation changes still reject.
Concurrent restore actions for same view cannot both apply under stale checks.
findings.existingTestGap: The controlled workspace helper supplies a mocked host.restore; existing38 cases cover defaultactivation,storage/material barriers and receipts, but do not execute this real App deferred refresh→composer overwrite sequence.

relatedObservation: Existing App restore guard also checks only text/knowledge/attachments, omitting profile/intent-only changes; address full material identity in the same fix, not a separatetask. Steering restore rejects nonempty targets but runs after other fields are already applied, so preflight affected material before committing application.
dispatch: Manager may assign original Recovery owner after its current read-only bounded research, using fresh original6ffv4/21 scopes. No sharedcontract/newtask needed. Browser/PG resources remain with Lead center restoration, no runtime grant.
cleanCode: Reviewed asynchronous ownership, complete draft integrity, and error paths using existing find-skills/codebase-design/clean-code methods; one concrete source race, no speculative broad refactor.
